analysis.title: Equities sell off despite good results
key_insights: With 3Q earnings season past the halfway point, results are good and mostly in line with UBS expectations. Equity volatility picked up because earnings momentum is slowing, not because of weak results.
S&P 500 EPS growth is on pace for nearly 30% y/y in 3Q, a deceleration from 2Q. Earnings revision breadth is likely starting to turn down from a high level, as UBS expected.
UBS says nothing heard this earnings season suggests downside risk to S&P 500 earnings has increased. AI capex remains robust, consumer spending is resilient and manufacturing is in an upswing.

Despite the poor Friday session, the S&P 500 is about 3.0% off its all-time high. The equal-weighted S&P 500 has rallied nearly 5.0% over the past month and is about 1.6% off its all-time high, so the aggregate market has held up.
77% of S&P 500 companies beat EPS estimates and 71% beat sales estimates, both better than the average since 2015. The median EPS beat is just under 4%, better than the historical trend.
UBS expects 3Q earnings growth for the median S&P 500 company at a low-double-digit rate. EPS estimate revisions for 4Q26 and 1Q27 are pacing better than typical seasonal patterns.

On AI, demand remains very strong and monetization is becoming more visible. Amazon and Alphabet reiterated 2026 capex guidance and suggested further increases in 2027. Microsoft trimmed 2026 capex guidance by 3% due to timing of third-party deliveries. Cloud revenue growth accelerated in 3Q from 2Q for all three, and backlogs kept growing.
UBS's AI TRIO recently raised their AI capex forecasts for 2026 to 2028.

Consumer spending is consistent. Visa saw steady spending across income segments with no deterioration in the lower-income cohort. MasterCard said sentiment is positive and consumers and businesses keep spending. Higher costs and inflation are becoming more pronounced, but companies can mostly offset them through pricing and other methods.
Industrial demand is resilient across the board, but higher freight costs are creating differences in margin profiles between businesses.
Just over 20% of S&P 500 market cap reports next week, led by Apple, in the second-busiest week of the season.

UBS stays constructive on US stocks. Uncertainties that could clarify in coming weeks: the Middle East situation, US elections, ability to raise capital for the AI build-out, and pace of AI revenue growth. UBS says investors seem increasingly braced for negative outcomes. S&P 500 targets of 8,100 (Dec 2026) and 8,400 (Jun 2027) remain intact.
earnings_insights: 3Q26 S&P 500 EPS growth on pace for nearly 30% y/y, a deceleration from 2Q (season past the halfway point, estimate-based pace, not final).
77% of S&P 500 companies beat EPS estimates and 71% beat sales estimates so far in 3Q26 (reported results to date).
Median EPS beat is just shy of 4% so far in 3Q26 (reported results to date). UBS expects median S&P 500 company 3Q EPS growth at a low-double-digit rate.

Microsoft trimmed 2026 capex guidance by 3% on timing of third-party deliveries. Amazon and Alphabet reiterated 2026 capex guidance and suggested further increases in 2027. Cloud revenue growth for all three accelerated in 3Q from 2Q.
Visa and MasterCard commentary points to steady consumer spending. Apple reports next week, with just over 20% of S&P 500 market cap reporting.
risk_factors: Slowing earnings momentum and turning revision breadth
Ability to raise additional capital for the AI build-out
Situation in the Middle East and US elections
Rising inflation and costs, which companies must offset through pricing
Higher freight costs creating margin differences among industrial companies

Earnings revision breadth is likely starting to turn down from a high level.

tension_points.bull_case: Results are good: 77% EPS beats, 71% sales beats, median EPS beat near 4%, and 4Q26 and 1Q27 estimate revisions are running better than normal. AI capex, consumer spending and manufacturing remain strong.
tension_points.bear_case: S&P 500 EPS growth is decelerating from 2Q and revision breadth is likely turning down from a high level, which UBS ties to the pickup in equity volatility.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Clarity on the Middle East, US elections, AI capital raising and AI revenue growth in coming weeks, which UBS says is not a sure positive.

theme_stances.key_argument: Earnings are good but growth is decelerating and revision breadth is turning down from a high level, with no sign of higher downside risk to earnings.
theme_stances.evidence: nothing we’ve heard this earnings season suggests that downside risk

theme_stances.key_argument: Demand remains exceptionally strong while monetization is becoming increasingly visible.
